mentions.name: Prompter Hawk
mentions.description: This is a dashboard for managing local coding agents such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Gemini CLI. Work is organized as non-interactive tasks (like "claude -p") whose outputs, such as lists of changed files and git commits, are attached to the task. It offers a glanceable dashboard for heavily parallelized agent work, persistent task data so a project can be reopened a month later with the same agents, and analytical views including counts of LOC, commits, and tool calls plus a timeline showing how much time each agent worked.
mentions.problem: Managing multiple Claude Code instances running in parallel across terminal windows is difficult.

mentions.name: Prompter Hawk
mentions.description: A task dispatch dashboard and GUI harness for AI coding agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, GPT) that replaces juggling multiple parallel agent terminals with a single AI task tracking board. Tasks are fire-and-forget with a parallelism-first workflow; the dashboard shows all parallel sessions, in-progress and queued tasks, and recent outputs. It tracks task status, file changes, and git commits, offers one-click task retry, cost-per-run breakdowns, scheduled recurring tasks, and a persistent local database of task history. It also provides timeline and analytics views (velocity, LOC and commit changes, most-read files, parallelization stats), automatic Mermaid system diagram generation during or after task execution, and agent-drafted task suggestions when agents are idle.
mentions.problem: Parallelizing AI agent work by running multiple claude code or codex terminals at once is unwieldy, and pulling up old chat histories is a poor way to track past tasks and outputs.
mentions.audience: Developers running multiple AI coding agent terminals in parallel
mentions.source_excerpt: Mainly I'm working on a task dispatch dashboard called Prompter Hawk that is designed to be the best UI for task management with agents.
